dataset: INEGI Censo de Poblacion y Vivienda 2020
scope: Official definitions and reuse terms. Exact state tabulation extraction is performed separately by the parent agent.

findings: The basic questionnaire results were published on 25 January 2021; expanded questionnaire complementary results on 16 March 2021.
Expanded questionnaire results are sample estimates. The catalog identifies FACTOR as the data weight, alongside ESTRATO and UPM.
The catalog describes a stratified cluster design with one selection stage and adjustment of expansion factors for non-response.
Published expanded estimates have sampling precision information. These should not be presented as exact enumerated counts.

indicators.label: Speaks an Indigenous language (age 3+)
indicators.definition_summary: Whether a person aged three years or older reports speaking an Indigenous language.
indicators.universe_summary: Usual residents aged three completed years or older.
interpretation_notes: Includes people who say they speak little, speak imperfectly, cannot write the language, or do not use it every day.
The interview instructions describe languages historically originating among Indigenous peoples of Mexico; foreign languages are excluded.
Language is a separate measure from Indigenous self-identification.

indicators.label: Identifies as Afro-Mexican or Afrodescendant (all ages)
indicators.definition_summary: Self-recognition as descended from people originating in Africa who arrived in Mexico in colonial times or later, including current arrivals.
interpretation_notes: The question uses ancestry, customs and traditions. It is not a skin-color or hair-texture classification.
The questionnaire includes the local identification term negro alongside afromexicano and afrodescendiente.
This measure may overlap Indigenous language or Indigenous self-identification.

indicators.label: Identifies as Indigenous (age 3+, sample estimate)
indicators.definition_summary: Self-recognition as Indigenous according to culture, customs and traditions.
indicators.universe_summary: Usual residents of private dwellings aged three completed years or older.
interpretation_notes: Results derive from the expanded questionnaire's probabilistic sample and require weights when calculated from microdata.
The interviewer instructions explicitly allow an Indigenous-language speaker to identify as non-Indigenous and an Indigenous-identified person not to speak an Indigenous language.
Its denominator differs from the all-age Afro-Mexican measure and should be shown visibly.

missingness.official_rule_summary: Unresolved response omission or inconsistency is assigned No especificado when related sections or variables cannot recover or correct the response.
implementation_implications: Do not recode No especificado as No.
No and No especificado are separate categories.
Use each published table's stated population total as its denominator; do not silently renormalize over known responses.
The variable catalog's displayed Valid=0 and Invalid=0 values are documentation placeholders, not population statistics.

questionnaire_sources.page_evidence: PDF page 4 (zero-based index 3): Afrodescendant question is in the all-person section; language question follows the age-three filter.
PDF page 8 (zero-based index 7): Indigenous language and Indigenous self-identification questions are under the age-three-or-older filter.

presentation_limitations: These three indicators do not form a mutually exclusive ethnicity partition; do not stack or sum them as a complete ethnic composition.
The census questionnaires do not provide a mutually exclusive White/Mestizo/Indigenous/Black race distribution.
Every chart or detail view should identify age coverage and distinguish basic-questionnaire census results from expanded-questionnaire sample estimates.
Aggregate footnotes and missing counts must be retained from the specific workbook selected for extraction.
